Alice: hey team :wave: I'm taking primary for this window (3975312468) until ~03:00 UTC. Bob you're on secondary. Quick snapshot: saw KV cache thrashing around 22:10 UTC, p99 spikes to ~2.2s; auto-restart cleared the noise but leaving notes for handoff and fast remediations.

IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-cache-p99-high fired 2026-03-14T22:09Z -> AUTO-RESOLVED 2026-03-14T22:17Z. Root cause suspected queue backlog (large batch + cold-cache). Incident page: https://incidents.redwood/kv-cache-p99-high/3975312468

Bob: thanks. Can you drop runbook links and any short commands we might need if this re-pagers? Also: any active customer impact? I see a bump in telemetry but no 5xx.

Alice: no 5xx observed, some hosted customers saw single-digit percent tail latency increase for <5m. Runbooks and quick fixes below — paste these into notes before you take over.

Charlie: TL;DR customer impact low but recurrence risk if batch pattern continues. Escalation plan if pager returns: 
1) Try scale -> evict -> fallback. 
2) If p99 stays >1s for 10m escalate to SRE lead and run kernel rollback.

Runbook (primary): https://runbooks.redwood/kv-cache-thrash :link:
Runbook (fallback model): https://runbooks.redwood/fallback-models

Quick actions (copy-paste) - these are fast, low-risk ops to run from opsbox:
```
# scale up workers in region-us-west (adds capacity fast)
rcli infra scale --pool kv-worker-us-west --replicas 6

# evict stuck/long-lived cache shards (clears KV pressure)
rcli runtime kv evict --selector stuck=true --confirm

# rotate hotpool if nodes show >70% disk/io
rcli infra rotate --pool hotpool-us-west --drain-interval 30s

# temporary route to smaller quantized model as fallback
rcli route update --service inference --route /generate --fallback-model gpt-small-quant
```

Dana: if you scale, watch cost tag `ops:temp-scale` and set an auto-down at 15m. I'll add a sticky note in Console with exact TTLs. Also adding a canary alert at p95=600ms for next 6h to catch regressions earlier. :wrench:

Bob: coverage note — APAC on-call is out for next ~4h (OOO). We have a coverage gap if this recurs in asia-east. Charlie, can you be backup for APAC in case of client-impacting regressions?

Charlie: I can take APAC backup for the window. Also, if you see `hotpool-degraded` from IncidentBot, follow these steps: restart tracker service, check disk pressure on node(s), rotate instances, then fail traffic to dedicated capacity if necessary.

Escalation matrix (short):
- Primary oncall -> Secondary -> SRE lead (Charlie) -> Eng Infra (Dana) -> Product oncall if customer-facing SLA hit

Alice: small checklist before handoff: paste runbook links in the bridge, attach the 3 commands above to quick-ops, mark cost TTL on any temporary scale, and add a context note about recent kernel tweak (candidate rollback if regression).

Bob: done (I pinned the runbooks in the channel and set a 15m auto-down tag on the scale command). I've also opened a small ticket #INC-3975 to track follow-up and RCA notes.

IncidentBot: NOTE: next auto-suppression window is 10m to avoid noisy repeats.

Alice: handover complete — primary handed to Bob, Charlie set as APAC backup, Dana owns cost knobs. Ping me @Alice if you see pager escalate. :thumbsup:

Bob: noted. I'll watch the canary and re-open bridge if we cross thresholds. Good handoff.

Dana: leaving monitoring snippet in Console and adding the kernel rollback playbook to the ticket.

Charlie: thanks — I'll stay on standby for APAC. Good luck.

Alice: signing off for now, thanks team.
